_fixture_note: WHY THIS CASE IS IN THE SET -- classify() was a pure function of (subject kind, verb) and the quote never reached it, so the graded IL-6 negative passed only because `reduces` happens to sit in DOWNSTREAM_EFFECT. That is one verb away from failing, and the verb it needs is one the upstream extractor is instructed to emit: claim-extraction/SKILL.md pins `how` to a CLOSED 11-verb list (binds inhibits activates increases decreases causes treats associated_with expressed_in measured_by no_relationship_stated), and `inhibits` is what that list gives you for 'inhibited IL-6 production'. Two links here, each with the verb pointing one way and its own quote the other. L20: `inhibits` (DIRECT_ACTION) on IL-6, quote is pure readout vocabulary. L21: `attenuates` (DOWNSTREAM_EFFECT) on IRAK4, quote is a purified-enzyme IC50. BEFORE: L20 silently nominates IL-6 as a target and L21 silently rejects IRAK4 as a readout -- one false positive and one false negative, both exit 0. AFTER: both go to `needs_adjudication` with `why_contested`, `verb_class` and `quote_reading`, and neither is nominated or rejected on the verb alone.
